sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: alcohol thresholds, refusal terms, first versus repeat DUI, DUI versus extreme DUI, aggravated DUI triggers and interlock checks
Look-alike thresholds, minimums and triggers from the DUI pages, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec20-R01 | anchor: A01
The on-the-spot loss of privilege starts at 0.08 for an ordinary driver but at 0.04 in a commercial vehicle that needs a commercial license, and any alcohol concentration can suspend a driver under 21. [A01]
Why it matters: group thresholds; difficulty three; confusable sec20-F10 versus sec20-F11 versus sec20-F13.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec20-R02 | anchor: A01
A first test refusal costs 12 months of privilege, while a second refusal within 84 months costs 24 months. [A01]
Why it matters: group refusal; difficulty three; prereq sec20-F14.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec20-R03 | anchor: A01
A first nitrous oxide offense means a 6-month suspension, while a second or later one means 12 months. [A01]
Why it matters: group nitrous oxide; difficulty two; confusable sec20-F03 versus sec20-F04.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec20-R04 | anchor: A01
A BAC under 0.08 is not a defense, because a driver can still be found guilty of driving while intoxicated. [A01]
Why it matters: group thresholds; difficulty two; prereq sec20-F12.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec20-R05 | anchor: A02
A first DUI means at least 10 consecutive days in jail and a 90-day minimum suspension, while a second DUI means at least 90 days in jail and a 12-month revocation. [A02]
Why it matters: group DUI tiers; difficulty three; confusable sec20-F16 versus sec20-F19.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec20-R06 | anchor: A02
Fines start at $1,250 for a first DUI, $2,500 for a first extreme DUI, $3,000 for a second DUI and $3,250 for a second extreme DUI. [A02]
Why it matters: group DUI fines; difficulty three; confusable sec20-F17 versus sec20-F22 versus sec20-F19 versus sec20-F25.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec20-R07 | anchor: A02
Extreme DUI begins at 0.15, and a higher tier at 0.20 raises the minimum jail to 45 days on a first offense and 180 days on a repeat, with no suspended sentence. [A02]
Why it matters: group extreme DUI; difficulty three; confusable sec20-F21 versus sec20-F23 versus sec20-F26.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec20-R08 | anchor: A02
For an ordinary first DUI the court may order an ignition interlock, while for a first extreme DUI the interlock is required. [A02]
Why it matters: group interlock orders; difficulty three; confusable sec20-F18 versus sec20-F24.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec20-R09 | anchor: A02
A third DUI within 7 years and a DUI with a passenger under 15 are both aggravated DUI, which carries prison for not more than 2 years. [A02]
Why it matters: group aggravated DUI; difficulty three; confusable sec20-F28 versus sec20-F30.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec20-R10 | anchor: A03
An interlock test happens before starting the engine and again at random intervals while driving. [A03]
Why it matters: group interlock use; difficulty two; confusable sec20-F33 versus sec20-F34.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec20-R11 | anchor: A03
The Executive Hearing Office hears challenges to MVD orders, most often orders suspending or revoking a license. [A03]
Why it matters: group hearings; difficulty one; prereq sec20-F38.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]
